title: Operations Coordinator
intro: Our design team does its best work when nothing is in the way — no missing files, no unclear next steps, no unsigned paperwork. This role keeps projects moving and the studio running, so designers can design and clients always know what happens next.
workOn: Monday kickoffs → Run the weekly kickoff. Check deadlines, flag risks, and make sure the team has everything it needs for the week.
Client calls → Open every project call with the agenda, keep time, and close with clear next steps.
Follow-ups → Send recap notes and action items to clients within hours of every call.
Asset chasing → Track down the files, access, and feedback the design team needs — before anyone is blocked.
Studio admin → Send contracts, NDAs, and invoices, and keep signatures and payments on track.
Lead follow-up → Keep new leads warm with timely, well-written follow-ups so no conversation goes quiet.
bring: 1–3 years as a project coordinator, studio coordinator, or account coordinator — agency experience preferred.
Obsessively organized. You never let a thread drop and you follow up without being asked.
Calm, clear presence on client calls.
Excellent written English — your recap emails are short, clear, and actionable.
Comfortable with admin: contracts, invoices, and e-signature tools.
Based in New York City and able to work from our studio.
niceToHave: Experience in a design or creative studio.
Familiarity with Notion, Slack, Figma, and invoicing tools.
howWeWork: Twice-weekly Slack updates keep pulses steady.
Small team, flat hierarchy, big ownership.
We meet once a year in different parts of the world to connect, plan, and reset.
applySteps: A short note on the most chaotic project you kept on track.
outro: If you’re the person who makes everyone else’s work easier, we’d love to meet you.
